onboarding.title: How Signature404 works
onboarding.subtitle: Decentralized freelance on Base — no middlemen, code enforces.
onboarding.step1_desc: Clients post jobs on the Job Board. Executors list services. Browse and respond to offers.
onboarding.step2_desc: Both parties agree to terms. A smart contract is deployed — this is your binding agreement.
onboarding.step3_desc: Client deposits USDC into the contract. Funds are locked on-chain — no one can touch them until conditions are met.
onboarding.step4_desc: Executor marks done. Client releases payment. No release after timeout? Funds auto-approve. Dispute? Arbiter resolves.
onboarding.step5_desc: You sign transactions, the platform pays gas. No ETH needed — just USDC for deal funding.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about Signature404 — the decentralized freelance protocol on Base.
faq.a_what_is: Signature404 is a decentralized freelance marketplace on Base. Clients post jobs, executors submit work, and funds are locked in an on-chain escrow contract — enforced by code, not by a platform admin.
faq.a_who_controls: No one. Funds are held by an autonomous smart contract. The platform cannot freeze, redirect, or touch your USDC. Only the client, executor, or arbiter can trigger state transitions — under conditions defined in the contract.
faq.a_is_free: Transactions are gasless — the platform relayer pays ETH gas fees on your behalf. You only spend USDC for the deal amount. A small platform fee is deducted on successful completion.
faq.a_wallets: MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Rainbow, Trust Wallet, Brave Wallet, OKX, Phantom, Ledger, and any injected wallet. WalletConnect lets you connect any mobile wallet.
faq.q_network: Which network does this run on?
faq.a_network: Currently deployed on Base Sepolia (testnet, chainId 84532). All USDC used is test USDC — no real money is at risk.
faq.a_how_deal:
1. Client creates a deal with executor address, amount, and deadline.
2. Client funds — USDC is locked in the contract.
3. Executor activates (accepts work).
4. Executor marks done.
5. Client releases payment — or raises a dispute.
6. If client is silent 5 days after delivery, funds auto-release.
faq.q_no_activate: What happens if the executor doesn't activate?
faq.a_no_activate: If the executor doesn't activate within 3 days after funding, the client can trigger a refund. Funds return to the client's wallet.
faq.q_deadline: What happens if the deadline passes?
faq.a_deadline: If the executor hasn't submitted work by the deadline, the client can trigger a timeout refund. Funds return to the client.
faq.a_cancel: The executor can decline before activating — client receives a refund after the 3-day window. Once active, no unilateral cancel; either party can raise a dispute instead.
faq.a_autoapprove: If the executor marks work done and the client doesn't respond for 5 days, funds automatically release to the executor. This prevents clients from holding payment hostage.
faq.a_gasless: You sign a message with your wallet (no ETH needed). The platform relayer submits the transaction on-chain and pays the gas fee. Your wallet only signs — it does not spend ETH.
faq.q_safe_sign: Is it safe to sign gasless messages?
faq.a_safe_sign: Yes. Each message is EIP-712 typed data bound to a specific contract, function, nonce, and deadline. The relayer cannot alter the call — it can only forward your signed intent.
faq.a_censored: If the relayer is down, you can always call the contracts directly using any Ethereum wallet or tools like cast. Gasless is a convenience layer, not a requirement.
faq.q_raise_dispute: How do I raise a dispute?
faq.a_raise_dispute: On the deal page, tap 'Raise Dispute'. USDC is frozen immediately. A registered arbiter will claim the case and review both sides.
faq.a_arbiters: Arbiters are addresses registered on-chain by the platform owner or chief arbiter. They are neutral third parties. You can view the full registry on the Arbiter page.
faq.q_claim: How does an arbiter claim a dispute?
faq.a_claim: Arbiters use a commit-reveal scheme: first commit a hash (to prevent front-running), then reveal in the next block to officially claim the deal. This ensures fair selection.
faq.q_outcomes: What are the possible dispute outcomes?
faq.a_outcomes: Client wins: full USDC refunded. Executor wins: full USDC paid to executor.
faq.q_arbiter_timeout: What if the arbiter doesn't resolve in time?
faq.a_arbiter_timeout: If the arbiter doesn't resolve within the arbiter window, either party can trigger an arbiter timeout — funds return to the client.
faq.a_job_post: A client posts a job with description, budget, and requirements. Executors apply. The client selects one and a deal is created.
faq.a_service: An executor lists a service with a fixed price. Clients browse and request it directly, creating a deal.
faq.a_nft: When a deal is successfully completed, the executor receives a soulbound NFT (non-transferable) as verifiable proof of the work. These build on-chain reputation over time.
faq.a_chat: Yes. All messages are end-to-end encrypted via XMTP. Only deal participants can read them — the platform cannot.
faq.q_files: Are files shared in chat private?
faq.a_files: Files are AES-256-GCM encrypted in your browser before upload. The encryption key travels only through XMTP (E2E encrypted). Files are stored on the server for 18 days, then permanently deleted.
faq.q_funds_safe: Can the platform take my funds?
faq.a_funds_safe: No. Smart contracts are immutable once deployed. The platform owner can upgrade protocol facets but cannot touch funds in individual Agreement contracts — those are standalone escrow contracts.
faq.a_audited: The protocol is on Base Sepolia testnet and has not been formally audited. Do not use with significant real funds until a mainnet audit is completed.
faq.a_diamond: Diamond is an upgradeable proxy pattern where a single proxy contract delegates calls to multiple 'facet' contracts. This allows the protocol to be extended or fixed without redeploying everything.
faq.a_source: Available on GitHub — see the link on the page.
faq.q_verify: How do I verify the deployed contracts?
faq.a_verify: Inspect all contracts on BaseScan. Diamond address: 0xF00CC71878c226E0b64253Fb71dD802aF12165D0
